original_test_intent: Verify that the intended AMI BMC implements the AutoVideoSettings OEM Redfish resource and returns a complete, syntactically valid, firmware-appropriate set of video-selection settings whose fields, types, enumerations and current values match the approved platform policy.
original_method: Select the unique row; identify BMC/SUT/WebUI/KVM/video topology and firmware; approve the exact OEM resource version/schema and expected current policy; authenticate through a protected TLS-validated Redfish session; GET the literal resource once; preserve status, response headers and raw body before duplicate-aware parsing; validate OData/OEM metadata, mandatory/optional properties, types, enumerations, ranges and cross-field constraints; correlate current values with read-only BMC Web/video behavior where approved; report missing/unsupported/mismatched data without PATCH, restart or display change.
manual_activity: Engineering supplies the firmware-specific OEM schema and expected platform video policy; the secure GET and typed validation are fully automatable.
required_inputs: BMC/SUT firmware and AMI OEM Redfish schema/resource revision
Mandatory/optional AutoVideoSettings properties, types, enumerations, ranges, defaults and cross-field constraints
Expected current values mapped to physical/BMC KVM/local-video topology and power states
Trusted TLS certificate/CA, protected authentication method and sensitive-field redaction policy
safety_requirements: Keep secrets out of URLs, logs, process output and artifacts
Capture raw status/headers/body before parsing and detect duplicate keys
Issue only GET; do not PATCH video policy, restart BMC/services or manipulate KVM/display state
Stop on wrong target, TLS/auth failure, unsupported resource, malformed/duplicate JSON or undefined expected value
agent_execution_scope: Perform one secure read-only GET of the exact resource and preserve raw evidence
Parse and validate approved schema, values and cross-field rules
Correlate with approved read-only inventory/UI evidence without changing video behavior
Do not weaken TLS, guess OEM semantics, modify settings/restart services or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve resource/schema revision and required versus optional fields
Approve expected values/enumerations/ranges and their physical/video-policy meaning
Approve permitted SKU/power-state exceptions and corroborating UI/inventory
Review discrepancies and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The endpoint and GET match the source and are read-only, but `-k` weakens identity and ordinary jq output cannot establish vendor correctness or preserve raw duplicate keys.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use a TLS-validated secret-safe Redfish client to save full status/headers/body from the exact AMI resource, then run duplicate-aware JSON and firmware-specific typed schema/value checks.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Exact AutoVideoSettings URI, read-only GET, readable/correct data criterion and 5/5-minute estimate remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Validate transport, raw JSON integrity, versioned OEM schema and platform-specific video-policy values as separate layers, retaining literal and normalized evidence for every field.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds endpoint trust, resource revision, duplicate detection, type/enum/range/cross-field oracle and video-topology correlation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A 2xx pretty-printed object can still contain wrong defaults, invalid combinations or fields that do not represent the installed video path; readability is not correctness.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: OEM property names/values may change by AMI firmware release or SKU, and some values may be dynamic by host power/KVM/local display state, so capture context with the response.

project_override_considerations: If the resource is legitimately absent for a non-AMI or unsupported SKU, engineering must record that applicability decision rather than treating 404 as pass. A WebUI view may corroborate policy but cannot silently replace the source-required OEM Redfish URI.
expected_evidence: TLS/client identity plus secret-redacted complete HTTP status/headers/raw body/hash
Approved read-only video-policy/UI corroboration and captured power/display context
No-write/no-restart audit, transport/schema exceptions and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require one exact OEM Redfish resource to be read and checked. The expected field/value set is missing but not contradictory.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The resource and read-only operation are explicit. Firmware-specific schema and expected values are supplyable validation data, so the case remains fully automatable.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2250 Wistron-BMC Sanity-00032-V001: approve the BMC/SUT/AMI firmware and `/redfish/v1/Managers/bmc/Oem/Ami/AutoVideoSettings` applicability/schema revision; mandatory/optional properties, types, enumerations, ranges, defaults and cross-field constraints; exact expected current values by video topology/SKU/host-power/KVM/local-display state; approve TLS/authentication, redaction and read-only UI/inventory corroboration.

review_improvement: Preserves the exact OEM resource check while replacing subjective readable JSON with a secure, versioned and topology-aware field/value oracle.
independent_technical_reasoning: An OEM resource is only meaningful relative to the firmware version and hardware video routing it controls. JSON validity and HTTP success establish availability, not whether the settings are semantically correct. Type, enumeration and cross-field validation can be fully automated once the project supplies the schema and current-state matrix. Because the operation is a GET, no user confirmation is needed, but endpoint trust and secret-safe authentication remain necessary to avoid collecting data from or exposing credentials to the wrong BMC.
